as_told.title: Corso's co-author inserted fake material into the book

plain: Podcast host Jesse Michels has said several times that Philip Corso, author of the 1997 book The Day After Roswell (about a supposed crashed craft near Roswell, New Mexico), was given only 24 hours by his co-author to edit the book. Michels says this explains why there is some nonsense in it. In one telling he names the co-author as William Birnes and mentions an earlier manuscript called Dawn of a New Age, and in another, crediting someone called UAP Gerb, he says the co-author may have slipped in false material to make Corso look bad. If so, it would mean the book's weaker parts are not Corso's own.
